questions.question: The five-year plans in India laid down not only specific objectives to be attained in the five years of a plan, but also what was to be achieved over a period of 20 years. This long-term plan is called a __________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**perspective plan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In India, the **long-term plans **that delineate specific objectives to be achieved over five years and 20 years are referred to as** perspective plans.**
 
• These plans enable adjustments in funding and projects to align with the nation's economic requirements.
 
• **Economic planning** in India entails the government's formulation of long-term strategies to develop and coordinate the economy efficiently.
 
• The first five-year plan was initiated in **1951**, marking the inception of India's planned development approach. Since then, the country has implemented twelve such plans.
 
• **The Planning Commission and the NITI Aayog** are responsible for devising, executing, and monitoring these plans.
 
• **The Prime Minister** serves as the** ex-officio chairman,** while the commission includes a nominated Deputy Chairman with the rank of a cabinet minister.
 
• The overarching objectives of the Five-Year Plans encompass achieving a high growth rate to enhance living standards, ensuring economic stability for prosperity, fostering a self-reliant economy, promoting social justice and reducing inequalities, and modernizing the economy to meet contemporary needs.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **From 1947 to 2017, **the Indian economy operated on the basis of planned development, which was facilitated through the implementation of **Five-Year Plans.**
 
• These plans were formulated, executed, and monitored by the Planning Commission from **1951 to 2014**, and subsequently by the** NITI Aayog** from **2015 to 2017.**
 
• The Prime Minister served as the ex-officio chairman of these commissions, while a nominated Deputy Chairman, holding the rank of a cabinet minister, assisted in their operations. Montek Singh Ahluwalia served as the** last Deputy Chairman of the Planning Commission,** resigning on **May 26, 2014.**
 
• The Twelfth Plan concluded its term in March 2017.

questions.question: What amount of ‘Seed Capital’ is provided as support to a Self-Help Group under the Pradhan Mantri Formalisation of Micro Food Processing Enterprises Scheme?
questions.solution:

__
 
• **The Pradhan Mantri Formalisation of Micro Food Processing Enterprises (PMFME) **scheme offers a grant of **Rs 40,000 **per member of a **Self-Help Group (SHG) **for working **capital and small tool purchases.**
 
• Each SHG can receive a total seed capital of Rs 40,000 per member, with a maximum cap of Rs 400,000 per SHG.
 
• This **seed capital** is provided as a grant to the SHG Federation by SRLM/SULM, which subsequently lends it to individual SHG members.

• Its primary objective is **to offer financial, technical, and business support** to enhance existing micro-food processing enterprises.
 
• The scheme provides credit-linked subsidies of up to Rs 10 lakh to facilitate the establishment or modernization of new micro food processing units.
 
• The PMFME scheme boasts a total outlay of Rs 10,000 crore spanning five years, from 2020-21 to 2024-25, with the aim of supporting 200,000 micro food processing units.

questions.question: How many planets are terrestrial planets?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**4**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The solar system **comprises **four terrestrial planets**:** Mercury, Venus, Earth, and Mars**, which also happen to be the four nearest to the sun.
 
• **Terrestrial planets**, also referred to as** "telluric planets"** or "rocky planets," feature a solid, rocky surface akin to Earth's terra firma.
 
• These planets typically possess a dense, metallic core primarily composed of iron, along with a silicate mantle layer.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• Within the Solar System, the **International Astronomical Union (IAU)** recognizes the terrestrial planets as the inner planets closest to the Sun: Mercury, Venus, Earth, and Mars.
 
• **Mercury, **the smallest planet in the Solar System, holds the position of the closest planet to the Sun.
 
• **Venus,** the second planet from the Sun, shares many similarities with Earth, being a terrestrial planet and comparable in mass and size to its neighboring planet.
 
• **Earth,** positioned as the third planet from the Sun, stands as a unique celestial body known for its capacity to support life. Its abundance of liquid surface water distinguishes it as a water world, a feature absent in other planets within the Solar System.
 
• **Mars**, known as the fourth planet from the Sun, earned the moniker "the Red Planet" due to the iron(III) oxide dust covering its surface, resulting in its distinctive orange-red appearance.

questions.question: Which winds blow across the Asian continent at latitudes north of the Himalayas roughly parallel to the Tibetan highlands?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Jet streams**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Jet streams** are **high-altitude winds** that traverse the **Asian continent **above the latitudes north of the Himalayas, running roughly parallel to the **Tibetan highlands**.
 
• The Tibetan highlands act as a dividing line, splitting the jet streams into north and south branches, with the northern branch significantly influencing **winter weather patterns** in India.
 
• These fast-flowing air currents are typically observed at altitudes of up to 3 km in the lower troposphere.
 
• Furthermore, at higher elevations, between 9 to 13 km above the Earth's surface, westerly winds persistently blow across Western and Central Asia from west to east.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The trade winds** are consistent winds that blow from east to west, occurring just north and south of the equator.
 
• **Southwest winds** carry warm air from the tropics and gradually cool as they travel northward over the sea.
 
• Northwest winds originate from the northwest direction and blow in a southeastward direction.

questions.question: Linthoi Chanambam is associated with which of the following sports events?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Judo**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Linthoi Chanambam, **an Indian judoka, achieved a historic feat by clinching the **gold medal in the 57 kg **women's event at the **2022 World Judo Cadets Championships held in Sarajevo.**
 
• Representing India with pride, she emerged as the** first-ever Indian medalist **in any age category of the World Championships.
 
• Hailing from Manipur, Linthoi Chanambam has showcased exceptional talent and determination in her judo journey.
 
• Prior to her remarkable victory at the World Championships, Linthoi Chanambam had already showcased her prowess on the judo mat by securing a gold medal at the Asian Cadet and Junior Judo Championships, which took place in Bangkok.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Judo,** a **modern Japanese martial art **and** combat sport,** has gained widespread recognition as an Olympic sport since its inclusion in the Games in 1964.
 
• Founded in **1882 by Kanō Jigorō,** judo stands out for its emphasis on "randori" (free sparring) over "kata" (pre-arranged forms), a departure from traditional martial arts.
 
• Judo excludes striking and weapon training elements, distinguishing it from its predecessors. In competitive judo, the primary objective is to defeat the opponent by executing throws, immobilizing them with a pin, or compelling them to submit through joint locks or chokes.
 
• With its origins deeply rooted in Japanese culture and tradition, judo has evolved into a globally recognized sport, promoting physical fitness, mental discipline, and respect among practitioners worldwide.

questions.question: In 2015, the eminent danseuse and ______________ exponent, Padma Subrahmanyam was selected for Kerala's prestigious choreography award 'Nishagandhi Puraskaram' instituted by the state tourism department.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bharatanatyam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **2015, Padma Subrahmanyam, **a renowned danseuse and **Bharatanatyam **exponent, was honored with **Kerala's** prestigious choreography award, the **'Nishagandhi Puraskaram,' **established by the state tourism department.
 
• This recognition reflects her exceptional contributions to the field of dance and choreography. Padma **Subrahmanyam's mastery of Bharatanatyam,** a classical Indian dance form, has earned her widespread acclaim and admiration.
 
• Her innovative choreography and dedication to preserving and promoting Indian classical dance traditions have made her a trailblazer in the field.
 
• The 'Nishagandhi Puraskaram' award acknowledges her outstanding artistic achievements and serves to celebrate her profound impact on the cultural landscape of India.
 
• Padma Subrahmanyam was honored with the **Padma Vibhushan in 2024,** the **Padma Bhushan in 2003, **and the **Padma Shri in 1981**, prestigious civilian awards of India, which rank among the highest recognitions bestowed by the nation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Bharatanatyam**, a classical Indian dance form originating in **Tamil Nadu,** stands as the most widely recognized classical dance style in India.
 
• Known for its precise movements, crisp lines, and expressive gestures, Bharatanatyam embodies the rich cultural heritage of South India.
 
• The dance form serves as a vehicle for conveying religious themes and spiritual concepts, particularly those associated with Shaivism and Hinduism in general.
 
• Traditionally performed as a collaborative art form, Bharatanatyam features a solo dancer accompanied by musicians and one or more vocalists.
 
• It encompasses a diverse range of themes, including religious narratives, secular subjects, and fusion styles that blend traditional and contemporary elements.

questions.question: In which year did Albert Einstein predict a new state of matter, the Bose-Einstein condensate (BEC), based on a quantum formulation by the Indian physicist Satyendra Nath Bose?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__1924.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Albert Einstein's **prediction of the **Bose-Einstein condensate (BEC) in 1924** was based on the quantum formulations put forth by Indian physicist **Satyendra Nath Bose**.
 
• This groundbreaking state of matter, often referred to as the** fifth state of matter,** was a result of Bose's foundational work on quantum mechanics in the early 1920s.
 
• Bose's contributions included the development of Bose-Einstein statistics and the theoretical framework for the BEC.
 
• The first** "pure" **BEC was subsequently created by Eric Cornell, Carl Wieman, and their colleagues at JILA on June 5, 1995.
 
• In a notable advancement, the **Cold Atom Laboratory experiment **conducted aboard the International Space Station achieved the creation of a BEC consisting of rubidium atoms in June 2020.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Satyendra Nath Bose, **an Indian mathematician and physicist, was highly regarded for his contributions to theoretical physics, particularly in the field of quantum mechanics during the early 1920s.
 
• His notable achievements include laying the groundwork for Bose-Einstein statistics and formulating the theory of the Bose-Einstein condensate.
 
• Recognized for his scholarly pursuits, Bose was elected as a Fellow of the Royal Society.
 
• In acknowledgment of his outstanding contributions to science, the Government of India conferred upon him the Padma Vibhushan, the nation's second highest civilian award, in 1954.

questions.question: Who among the following was the first president of IOC?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Demetrius Vikelas**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Demetrius Vikelas (1805–1908)** served as the inaugural president of the **International Olympic Committee (IOC)** from 1894 to 1896, holding the distinction of having the shortest tenure among all IOC presidents, **spanning just two years.**
 
• A Greek businessman and writer, Vikelas **co-founded the IOC **alongside Pierre de Coubertin in 1894.
 
• In addition to his involvement in sports administration, Vikelas made significant contributions to education.
 
• In **1893, **he established the Institut Melas, an institution dedicated to providing preschool education in regions of Greece beyond Athens.
 
• Vikelas is often characterized as the most cosmopolitan, internationally-minded, and erudite president in the history of the IOC.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• The International Olympic Committee (IOC), a non-governmental sports organization, is responsible for organizing the **modern Olympic Games,** which occur every two years, alternating between the summer and winter editions.
 
• The president of the IOC typically serves two terms of four years each, with the possibility of renewal once, allowing them to oversee at least two Summer and two Winter Olympic Games during their tenure.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Michael Morris**, 3rd Baron Killanin, was an Irish journalist, author, sports official, and the sixth President of the International Olympic Committee.
 
• **Pierre de Coubertin, **also known as Baron de Coubertin, was a French educator and historian, renowned as the co-founder of the International Olympic Committee and its second president. He is widely regarded as the father of the modern Olympic Games.
 
• **Avery Brundage** was an American sports administrator who held the position of the fifth president of the International Olympic Committee from 1952 to 1972.

questions.question: Who among the following was the successor of Mughal emperor Shahjahan to the throne?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Aurangzeb**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Aurangzeb, **the** successor of Mughal emperor Shah Jahan**, ascended to the throne after a succession struggle among his four sons in 1657.
 
• He declared himself emperor in 1658, succeeding Shah Jahan, who had fallen ill.
 
• Despite Shah Jahan's recovery from illness, Aurangzeb emerged victorious and imprisoned him in the Agra Fort until his death in 1666.
 
• Aurangzeb ruled the Mughal Empire from **1658 to 1707, **marking a significant period in Indian history.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Mirza Shahab-ud-Din Muhammad Khurram, **also known as** Shah Jahan I, **was the **fifth Mughal Emperor,** reigning from 1628 until 1658.
 
• His rule marked the pinnacle of the Mughal Empire's architectural and cultural achievements.
 
• As the third son of Jahangir, Shah Jahan actively participated in military campaigns against the Sisodia Rajputs of Mewar and the rebellious Lodi nobles of the Deccan.
 
• Upon Jahangir's death in October 1627, Shah Jahan emerged victorious in a power struggle against his youngest brother, Shahryar Mirza, and ascended to the throne, crowning himself emperor in the Agra Fort.

questions.question: How many fundamental rights were provided originally by the Indian Constitution in 1950?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Seven**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Constitution originally provided **seven main fundamental rights,** encompassing the right to equality, freedom, protection against exploitation, freedom of religion, cultural and educational rights, right to property, and the right to constitutional remedies.
 
• However, the right to property was removed from **Part III **of the Constitution through the **44th Amendment in 1978**.
 
• **Fundamental Rights**, enshrined in Part III of the Constitution, serve to uphold individual liberty and democratic principles grounded in the equality of all members of society.
 
• These rights guarantee civil liberties to all citizens and prevent the State from infringing upon individual liberty, while also obligating it to safeguard citizens' rights from encroachment by society.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The Fundamental Rights, Directive Principles of State Policy, and Fundamental Duties **are integral components of the Constitution of India, delineating the fundamental obligations of the state towards its citizens and the reciprocal duties and rights of citizens towards the State.
 
• These provisions were crafted by the Constituent Assembly of India during the constitution-making process between 1949.
 
• Fundamental Rights, outlined in Part III of the Indian Constitution **(Articles 12 to 35), **ensure equality before the law and prohibit discrimination based on various factors such as race, place of birth, religion, caste, creed, sex, or gender. These rights are enforceable by the courts, with certain limitations.
 
• The **Directive Principles of State Policy,** laid down in Part IV of the Constitution, serve as guidelines for the government in formulating laws and policies.

questions.question: Which ports belong to the western coast of India?

options.text: Kandla port, Mormugao port, Kolkata port
Kandla port, Mormugao port, Kochi port
Kandla port, Mormugao port, Chennai port
Kandla port, Haldia port, Kochi port

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kandla port, Mormugao port, Kochi port**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kandla port, Mormugao port, Kochi ports **belong to the western coast of India.
 
• **Kandla Port:**
 
 
• Located in the Kutch district of Gujarat, Kandla port is one of the largest ports in India and plays a crucial role in the country's trade activities.
 
• It serves as a major hub for exporting various goods, including petroleum products, grains, salt, and textiles.
 
• Kandla port is strategically positioned near the Gulf of Kutch, offering easy access to international shipping routes.
 
 
 
• **Mormugao Port:**
 
 
• Situated in Mormugao, Goa, Mormugao port is another significant port on the western coast of India.
 
• It primarily handles the export of iron ore, manganese ore, and other minerals mined in the region.
 
• Mormugao port is known for its natural harbor, which allows for the smooth movement of large cargo ships.
 
 
 
• **Kochi Port:**
 
 
• Kochi port, located in the city of Kochi (formerly Cochin) in Kerala, is a major maritime gateway on the western coast.
 
• It is one of the oldest ports in India and serves as a key center for international trade, particularly in the southern region.
 
• Kochi port handles a diverse range of cargo, including spices, seafood, coir, and containerized goods.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• Stretching approximately **1,500 kilometers** in length and measuring between 10 to 25 kilometers in width, these plains are a significant geographical feature of the region.
 
• The western coastal plains are characterized by their division into three distinct parts: the Canara coast, the Konkan coast, and the Malabar coast.
 
• Each of these regions has its own unique topographical and cultural attributes.

questions.question: What do you call the drugs that bind to the receptor site and inhibit its natural function?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__ **Antagonists.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Antagonist** is a chemical substance that binds to and block the activation of certain receptors on cells, preventing a biological response.
 
• **Example: Naloxone is a competitive antagonist for the opioid receptor**
 
• These are the substances that reduce **arousal and stimulation.**

 
• They affect the** central nervous system**, slowing down the messages b/w the brain and body.
 
• They can affect concentration and coordination b/w and slow down the activity of a person to some extent.
 
• **As the name indicates these are the drugs used to depress the actions.​**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Antidepressants: **

 
 
• These are the drugs used to treat or prevent clinical depression.
 
• They can also be used to treat some other conditions, including. 
 
• Observing compulsive disorder.
 
• generalized anxiety disorder.
 
• Post-traumatic stress disorder
 
• Sometimes it is used to treat people with long-term chronic pain.
 
 
 
• **Agonist: **
 
 
• It is a drug or chemical substance that binds with a receptor and activates it to induce the action or response.
 
• These have an intrinsic efficacy and affinity for the receptor that results in binding to it.
 
• This binding results in changes in the receptors' functioning in the host cells.

questions.question: Who among the following designed a campaign that came to be known as the ‘Rowlatt Satyagraha’?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mahatma Gandhi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mahatma Gandhi** spearheaded the **Rowlatt Satyagraha campaign**, a **pivotal chapter** in India's struggle for independence.
 
• This **non-violent civil disobedience movement** unfolded in** 1919 **as a response to the Rowlatt Act, an oppressive law enacted by the** British colonial government.**
 
• The act granted authorities the authority to detain individuals without trial for up to two years, a measure deemed unjust and repressive by Gandhi and his supporters.
 
• Gandhi, recognizing the urgency of opposing this** draconian legislation**, called for a nationwide hartal, or strike, to denounce the Rowlatt Act.
 
• The response was resounding, with the hartal gaining widespread support and catalyzing a wave of demonstrations and protests throughout India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The Rowlatt Satyagraha** served as a potent catalyst in raising awareness about the injustices perpetuated by British rule.
 
• It underscored the efficacy of non-violent resistance as a formidable tool in the fight for freedom and equality.
 
• Moreover, the movement marked a personal triumph for Gandhi, showcasing his leadership prowess and charismatic influence over the Indian populace.
 
• The Rowlatt Satyagraha stands as a testament to the indomitable spirit of the Indian people and their unwavering commitment to securing their rights and liberties through peaceful means.

questions.question: Who among the following was the Vice President of the Interim Government formed by Congress in 1946?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Jawaharlal Nehru.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Jawaharlal Nehru** served as the **Vice President of the Interim Government** established by the **Congress in 1946**.
 
• This interim administration came into existence on September 2, 1946, and comprised members selected from the newly elected Constituent Assembly.
 
• The **Congress Party secured 208 seats **in the assembly, while the Muslim League won 73 seats.
 
• Jawaharlal Nehru, as the Vice President of the Council, wielded powers akin to those of a Prime Minister.
 
• This interim arrangement persisted until **August 15, 1947**, when India and Pakistan gained independence from colonial rule.
 
• During this period, **Maulana Abul Kalam Azad** was appointed to lead the Department of Education. Additionally, with the inclusion of the Muslim League in the Interim Government, the Department of Finance was helmed by Liaquat Ali Khan.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• Initially overseen by the **Viceroy of India**, it was restructured into a council of ministers, with the **Vice-President of the Council, Jawaharlal Nehru,** assuming the powers akin to those of a Prime Minister.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is NOT true for Indian monsoons?

options.text: Monsoonal rainfall is affected by jet streams
Monsoonal rainfall is the lifeline of Indian agriculture
Himalayas play an important role in monsoonal rainfall
Monsoonal rainfall is not affected by the relief features of the country

questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Monsoonal rainfall is not affected by the relief features of the country **is** NOT true for Indian monsoons.**
 
• Monsoonal rainfall in India is indeed influenced by various geographical and atmospheric factors, including relief features such as mountains and plateaus.
 
• **For example, **mountains like the **Western Ghats and the Eastern Ghats** influence rainfall distribution through orographic lifting, while coastal areas often experience different rainfall patterns due to their proximity to the sea. Overall, relief features play a crucial role in shaping the spatial distribution of monsoonal rainfall across India.
 
• Therefore, statement 4, which suggests that monsoonal rainfall is not affected by relief features, is not accurate.

• **Monsoonal rainfall is affected by jet streams: **This statement is true. Jet streams, particularly the subtropical westerly jet stream, play a significant role in the onset, intensity, and distribution of monsoonal rainfall in India. Changes in the position and strength of jet streams can influence the behavior of monsoon systems.
 
• **Monsoonal rainfall is the lifeline of Indian agriculture:** This statement is true. Monsoonal rainfall is crucial for agriculture in India, as it provides the majority of the water needed for crop cultivation. The timely arrival and distribution of monsoon rains are essential for crop growth and overall agricultural productivity.
 
• **Himalayas play an important role in monsoonal rainfall:** This statement is true. The Himalayan mountain range acts as a barrier to the moisture-laden monsoon winds coming from the Indian Ocean. As these winds encounter the Himalayas, they are forced to rise, leading to orographic rainfall on the windward side of the mountains. This process significantly contributes to the overall monsoonal rainfall pattern in India.

questions.question: How many fundamental rights were there at the time of adoption of the Indian Constitution?

• **The Constitution** initially outlined **seven main fundamental rights,** covering equality, freedom, protection against exploitation, freedom of religion, cultural and educational rights, the right to property, and the right to constitutional remedies.
 
• However, the right to property was eliminated from Part III of the Constitution via the **44th Amendment in 1978.**
 
• Fundamental Rights, as articulated in** Part III of the Constitution,** uphold individual liberty and democratic principles grounded in societal equality.
 
• These rights guarantee civil liberties to all citizens and prevent the State from infringing upon individual liberty, while also mandating it to protect citizens' rights from societal encroachment.

• These provisions were crafted by the Constituent Assembly of India during the constitution-making process between 1949.
 
• Fundamental Rights, detailed in Part III of the Indian Constitution (Articles 12 to 35), ensure equality before the law and prohibit discrimination based on various factors such as race, place of birth, religion, caste, creed, sex, or gender. These rights are enforceable by the courts, subject to certain limitations.
 
• **The Directive Principles of State Policy,** enshrined in** Part IV** of the Constitution, serve as guiding principles for the government in formulating laws and policies.

questions.question: The main function of centriole is:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Centrioles** are paired** barrel-shaped organelles f**ound in the **cytoplasm of animal cells**, typically situated near the **nuclear envelope**.
 
• They play a crucial role in organizing **microtubules**, which act as the cell's structural framework.
 
• Additionally, centrioles aid in determining the positioning of the nucleus and other organelles within the cell.
 
• Each centriole resides within the centrosome, an area of the cytoplasm located adjacent to the nucleus.
 
• The centrosome, considered an organelle, contains two centrioles.
 
• Composed of microtubules, centrioles are integral to cell division processes and are essential for maintaining cellular structure and function.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Centrioles **consist of **nine groups of microtubule triplets** arranged in a cylindrical configuration, a detailed structure that can only be observed under an electron microscope.
 
• These microtubule triplets are interconnected and oriented at right angles to each other, contributing to the centriole's overall stability and function.
 
• However, there are exceptions to this typical centriolar organization. For instance, in the embryos of Drosophila melanogaster, nine pairs of microtubules are formed instead of the usual microtubule triplets.
 
• Similarly, premature embryos and sperm cells of Caenorhabditis elegans exhibit a unique arrangement of nine single microtubules, deviating from the standard centriolar structure observed in most animal cells.

questions.question: In 1957, who redefined a model that predicted the shape of individual molecules based on the extent of electron-pair electrostatic repulsion?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Nyholm and Gillespie**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ronald Gillespie and Ronald Nyholm **significantly enhanced the **valence shell electron pair repulsion (VSEPR) model** in **1957,** refining its level of detail and its ability to discern between various molecular geometries.
 
• The **VSEPR theory** represents a **foundational concept in chemistry,** offering a straightforward explanation for the shapes of molecules.
 
• It posits a direct relationship between molecular geometry and the count of valence electrons, further providing predictions for precise molecular structures, including bond angles.
 
• The theory was initially proposed by **Nevil Sidgwick and Herbert Powell** in 1940, yet its roots trace back to Ryutaro Tsuchida of Japan, who originally suggested the notion of a correlation between molecular geometry and the number of valence electron pairs in 1939.
 
• However, it was the contributions of Gillespie and Nyholm that significantly expanded and refined the VSEPR model, solidifying its position as a fundamental tool in the study of molecular structures.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The VSEPR model**, or the Valence Shell Electron Pair Repulsion model, offers predictions for** the geometry of the majority of polyatomic molecules and ions.**
 
• It achieves this by solely considering the count of electron pairs surrounding the central atom, while disregarding all other valence electrons.
 
• According to the model, **lone pairs of electrons localize** on the central atom, while each bonded pair is shared between two atoms.
 
• The lone pair electrons in a molecule occupy a larger spatial region compared to the bonding pairs of electrons.
 
• Also referred to as the Gillespie-Nyholm theory, the VSEPR theory is named after its principal developers, Ronald Gillespie and Ronald Nyholm.

• Notably,** prokaryotic cells **lack membrane-bound organelles characteristic of eukaryotic cells, such as mitochondria or endoplasmic reticulum.

• **Ribosomes** are large ribonucleoprotein complexes found ubiquitously in all cells. Comprising both RNA and proteins, ribosomes play a crucial role in translating genetic information stored in mRNA into polypeptide chains.
 
• **Plasmids** are small, extrachromosomal DNA molecules present within a cell, physically distinct from the chromosomal DNA and capable of replicating independently. They often carry non-essential genes that may confer advantages such as antibiotic resistance.
 
• Discovered in 1897 by Italian physician Camillo Golgi, the Golgi complex is a cellular organelle consisting of five to eight flattened membrane-bound sacs known as cisternae. It plays a vital role in processing, modifying, and packaging proteins and lipids for transport within the cell or secretion outside the cell.

questions.question: What is the name of the Comprehensive Household Survey providing labour force statistics in India, which was first conducted in 1955?

• **The Employment-Unemployment Survey (EUS)** is India's most extensive **survey for labor force statistics**, originating in the **9th round of the National Sample Survey (NSS)** in **1955**.
 
• It transitioned to quinquennial surveys, beginning with the **27th round in 1972-73**, following recommendations from the **M. L. Dantwala committee report.**
 
• Over the years, eight quinquennial surveys have been conducted, with the most recent one in 2011-12.
 
• The EUS survey spans an entire year to capture seasonal fluctuations in employment. It assesses economic activity over three reference periods: yearly, weekly, and daily.
 
• These reference periods correspond to three activity statuses: **Usual Status (US), Current Weekly Status (CWS), and Current Daily Status (CDS).**
 
• The Usual Status definition is the broadest measure of employment, while the Daily Status definition is the most conservative.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
